answer: Assign each new identity a randomized maturation delay before any power activates, drawn from beacon randomness bound to its key, so neither compute nor capital can shorten it. A farm minting a cohort of fakes in one instant gets N independent draws scattered across a long horizon — they cannot ripen together to strike as one pulse, and the burst disperses like a tide pulling back. Each head must survive to its own wake epoch to taste any nectar of influence. Honest agents wait out one delay; attackers gain no synchronized mass, since time gates it and randomness forbids coordination.
